title: Log Reader
body:
Goal: teach Python to read the list of save points that git log --oneline prints, like this:

9c1e2d4 Add high score file
5b7a913 Fix hero walking through walls
0f9e8d7 Start game project

The first word of each line is the commit id. The rest is the message. Git shows the newest commit at the top.

  1. Open starter.py in Thonny. parse_line is already done - read it first.
  2. Finish the four TODOs: parse_log, count_commits, find_commits and oldest_first.
  3. Press Run. You should see:
This project has 5 commits.
The story of the project, from the beginning:
  1. Start game project
  2. Draw first level
  ...
Commits about the hero: ['5b7a913', '2d4f6a8']

Extra: in Terminal, inside your git-quest folder, type git log --oneline, copy the lines, and paste them into SAMPLE_LOG (between the """ marks). Run again to read YOUR history.

hints.label: Hint 1
hints.title: Where to look
hints.html: Read parse_line first, since it is already done. It turns one line into a pair: the commit id and the message. The other three jobs all start by turning the whole text into a list of those pairs.

hints.label: Hint 2
hints.title: Try this
hints.html: text.splitlines() gives you a list of lines. Loop over it, skip any line that is empty, and use parse_line on the rest. For the later jobs, call parse_log(text) instead of repeating yourself. Lists have a .reverse() method.

hints.label: Hint 3
hints.title: Almost there
hints.html: Unpack each pair in the loop like this: for ____, ____ in parse_log(text):. Then use if to test the message, and .append(____) to collect the right piece. For the last job, collect first, then reverse the list before you return.

# Log Reader - YOUR version
# Reads the text that "git log --oneline" prints. Each line looks like:
#     9c1e2d4 Add high score file
# The first word is the commit id (a short "hash"); the rest is the message.
# Finish the TODOs, then press Run and see if it does what the README says.

SAMPLE_LOG = """9c1e2d4 Add high score file
5b7a913 Fix hero walking through walls
2d4f6a8 Add jump to hero
a1b2c3d Draw first level
0f9e8d7 Start game project
"""


def parse_line(line):
    """Split one log line into a tuple (commit_id, message). (Already done!)"""
    parts = line.strip().split(" ", 1)  # split only at the FIRST space
    commit_id = parts[0]
    if len(parts) > 1:
        message = parts[1]
    else:
        message = ""
    return (commit_id, message)


def parse_log(text):
    """Turn the whole log text into a list of (commit_id, message) tuples."""
    commits = []
    # TODO 1: loop over text.splitlines(). For every line that is not empty,
    #         append parse_line(line) to commits.
    return commits


def count_commits(text):
    """How many save points are in the log?"""
    # TODO 2: use parse_log and len
    return 0


def find_commits(text, word):
    """Return the ids of commits whose message contains word (any capitals)."""
    ids = []
    # TODO 3: loop over parse_log(text). If word.lower() is in message.lower(),
    #         append the commit id to ids.
    return ids


def oldest_first(text):
    """git log shows the NEWEST commit first. Return the messages oldest first."""
    messages = []
    # TODO 4: collect every message, then reverse the list
    return messages


if __name__ == "__main__":
    print(f"This project has {count_commits(SAMPLE_LOG)} commits.")
    print("The story of the project, from the beginning:")
    for number, message in enumerate(oldest_first(SAMPLE_LOG), start=1):
        print(f"  {number}. {message}")
    print("Commits about the hero:", find_commits(SAMPLE_LOG, "hero"))
